subject: logistic regression (stat_smooth) and flipped boxplots in combination

messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: logistic regression (stat_smooth) and flipped boxplots in combination
parts:
Hi,

I have a variable (measuremnent) that is grouped into two groups (0,1). For their relation I use a logistic regression (glm, binomial).
Now I'd like to plot them and the corresponing regression line. That works fine, but is there also the possibility to add boxplots to
the plot. For better understanding a small working example:

df <- data.frame(Y=c(rep(0,50),rep(1,50)),X=c(rnorm(50,3),rnorm(50,5)))

pl1 <- ggplot(df,aes(x=X,y=Y))+
    geom_point()+
    stat_smooth(aes(x=X,y=Y),method="glm",family="binomial")

pl2 <- ggplot(df,aes(x=as.factor(Y),y=X))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_boxplot()+
  coord_flip()

In the end I'd like to combine both plots including boxes and the regression line. Is something like that possible?

Thanks for your help!
/J

> df <- data.frame(Y=c(rep(0,50),rep(1,50)),X=c(rnorm(50,3),rnorm(50,5)))
>
> pl1 <- ggplot(df,aes(x=X,y=Y))+
> geom_point()+
> stat_smooth(aes(x=X,y=Y),method="glm",family="binomial")
>
> pl2 <- ggplot(df,aes(x=as.factor(Y),y=X))+
> geom_point()+
> geom_boxplot()+
> coord_flip()
>

You can't 'add' two ggplot objects together in the way you're
suggesting - however, you could do something similar in lattice and
use the '+' operator in latticeExtra to superimpose one on the other
as long as the x/y scales are similar in both trellis objects.

The usual way to visualize the result of a (one-variable) logistic
regression is to plot the predicted values on the response scale
[predict(..., type = "response"), which lie between 0 and 1] vs. x and
then use rug plots to display the points at y = 0 and y = 1
(geom_rug). Rug plots are often more effective than boxplots because
they show more detail about the x-positioning of the success and
failure events.

Dennis
